thread.title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Dow Faces Nearly 200-point Drop As Trump Ups The Ante In Trade Hostilities

author: morningstar.com
title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Dow Faces Nearly 200-point Drop As Trump Ups The Ante In Trade Hostilities
text:
By Barbara Kollmeyer, MarketWatch
Monthly jobs data ahead, and Fed chief Powell to speak
U.S. stocks looked set to snap a three-session string of wins on Friday, as President Donald Trump's administration delivered a fresh bout of volatility in the market, with a proposal that amplifies recent tariff threats against China, reviving market rattling trade anxieties.
Trump announced late Thursday that he was considering tariffs on another $100 billion in Chinese goods, which would triple the amount of imports facing levies.
Meanwhile, traders are looking ahead to two big economic events Friday--the release of U.S. March payroll data and a speech by Federal Reserve Chairman Jerome Powell.
What are main benchmarks doing?
Paring some of a deeper, earlier loss, Dow Jones Industrial Average futures fell 178 points, 0.7%, to 24,290. S&P 500 futures dropped 16.35 points, or 0.6%, to 2,645. Nasdaq-100 futures fell 41.50 points, or 0.6%, to 6,558.75.
The major U.S. stock indexes posted their first three-day gain in a month (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-stocks-set-up-for-more-gains-as-trade-fears-stay-muted-2018-04-05) on Thursday, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average climbing 241 points, or 1%, to 24,505. The S&P 500 index rose 0.7%, while the Nasdaq Composite Index added 0.5%.
Equities fell hard Monday, then proceeded to recover, but Friday's session is promising volatility to which investors are becoming accustomed. With one more session to go, Dow is looking at a gain of 1.7% for the week, while the S&P 500 is poised to put on 0.8%. A weekly advance for the Nasdaq is on the line, with the index up just 0.2% as of Thursday's close.
Read:Dimon: Investors underestimate threat of 'drastic action' by Fed, other central banks (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/jpmorgans-dimon-investors-beware-drastic-action-by-fed-other-central-banks-2018-04-05)
What's driving markets
The White House said in a statement (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/trump-statement-requesting-100-billion-in-additional-china-tariffs-2018-04-05) after the market close Thursday that Trump has asked the U.S. Trade Representative to consider an extra $100 billion in Chinese goods to face tariffs (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/futures-fall-as-trump-seeks-100-billion-in-additional-china-tariffs-2018-04-05) and to identify the products that could be targeted.
The move escalates a tit-for-tat trade battle between the two biggest economies in the world: In an escalating trade skirmish, both countries have each proposed levies on $50 billion in imports from the other. Just a day ago, stocks moved higher on hopes a full-blown trade war could be averted once negotiations began.
Read:Republican senator on Trump's latest tariff threat: 'This is nuts' (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/republican-senator-on-trumps-latest-tariff-threat-this-is-nuts-2018-04-05)
U.S. stock futures immediately tumbled on Thursday's news, action which continued into Friday's session, though losses weren't as severe as in reactions to other, recent trade rumblings. China's commerce department responded to the latest tariff threat by saying it respond with countermeasures if needed.
"The Chinese side will follow suit to the end, not hesitate to pay any price, resolutely counterattack and take new comprehensive measures in response," said a ministry statement via its website (http://www.mofcom.gov.cn/article/ae/ag/201804/20180402728771.shtml), citing an unnamed spokesman. The statement added that China "doesn't want" a trade war, but is not afraid to fight one."
"If this trade war comes to pass, it will be an evenly matched total war between China and the U.S. economies, and not some small scuffle. It would be delusional for the U.S. to think it will be victorious at the end of this trade war," China's state-run Global Times said in opinion editorial (http://www.globaltimes.cn/content/1096648.shtml).
Away from trade, Friday should see the release of monthly U.S. jobs data, which are slated to be released at 8:30 a.m. Eastern Time, and are expected to reflect a slowdown in the pace of jobs growth, which has run somewhat hot in the first three months of 2018.
Also on deck are comments from Fed Chairman Jerome Powell, who is set to speak to the Economic Club of Chicago at 1:30 p.m. Later, San Francisco Fed President John Williams is scheduled to give a speech in Santa Rosa, Calif., at 4 p.m.
Which economic reports are in focus?
Economists polled by MarketWatch are forecasting an increase of 170,000 in nonfarm payrolls in March, far below February's massive 313,000 gain. Economists also forecast a 0.2% rise in hourly pay, which would nudge the annual gain up to 2.7%, from 2.6%.
Read:U.S. job gains in March probably will suffer from weather-related hangover (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/the-good-weather-will-be-bad-news-for-the-march-jobs-report-2018-04-05)
An update on consumer credit for February is due at 3 p.m. Eastern.
Check out:MarketWatch's Economic Calendar (http://www.marketwatch.com/economy-politics/calendars/economic)
What are strategists saying?
"While the tariffs story will likely continue to be the main mover of financial markets, we can't ignore the data that's about to be released. The U.S. jobs report is arguably the most important economic report we get each month and offers valuable insight into how the labor market is performing and, more importantly right now, whether wages are growing," said Craig Erlam, senior market analyst at OANDA, in a note to clients.
Erlam added that an "upside surprise" will get investors thinking about the chances that higher inflation is en route.
Opinion:Stock guru who called S&P 500 gains sees no new market high before October (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/stock-guru-who-called-sp-500-gains-sees-no-new-market-high-before-october-2018-04-06)
What stocks are moving?
Salesforce.com Inc.(CRM) shares were down 1% in premarket trading after the cloud-computing company confirmed late Thursday it will issue $2.5 billion in bonds to help finance its purchase
Shares of Micron Technology Inc.'s stock(MU) slid 3.6% in premarket trading a day after UBS initiated coverage of the semiconductor group with a sell rating. And those analyst said the semiconductor industry will face headwinds this year (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/micron-nvidia-weigh-as-chip-makers-hamper-tech-gains-2018-04-05).
In the same sector, Nvidia Corp.(NVDA) was down nearly 1% in premarket. Short seller Citron Research on Thursday tweeted that it sees shares falling below $200 soon.
Target Corp.(TGT) has agreed to pay more than $3.7 million (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/target-to-pay-37-million-to-settle-suit-over-racial-bias-in-job-screening-2018-04-05) to settle a lawsuit over racial bias in screening job applicants. The retailer also said it would overhaul its job-screening guidelines. Shares of the retailer weren't being actively traded in the premarket.
Apple Inc.(AAPL) shares slipped 0.8% in premarket. Court documents revealed Thursday that Chief Executive Tim Cook will be deposed (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/apple-ceo-tim-cook-to-be-deposed-in-qualcomm-lawsuit-2018-04-05) on June 27 in chipmaker Qualcomm Inc.'s(QCOM) lawsuit against the iPhone maker. Apple's stock was down 1.1% in premarket trade.
What are other markets doing?
Asian stocks had a mixed day (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/asian-markets-waver-after-trumps-latest-broadside-against-china-2018-04-05), with the Hong Kong Hang Seng Index rising 1% on bets that the latest Trump tariff threat may not develop into any real issue.
After logging strong advances on Thursday, European stocks fell across the board (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/european-markets-tip-lower-as-trade-worries-resurface-to-rattle-investors-2018-04-06). Gold futures eased modestly, while the ICE U.S. Dollar Index was flat. A pullback for perceived riskier assets took a toll on oil prices , which fell 0.4%.
